factors.label: Insider trading
factors.description: Timing, percentage of holdings, baseline trading and trading-plan context; sales alone are not dispositive.
questions: Which defendant sold, when, and how much of available holdings?
What was the prior trading baseline and any plan adoption or amendment date?

factors.label: Confidential witnesses
factors.description: Separate source reliability from whether the reported facts actually concern scienter.
questions: What job title, duties, reporting line and tenure are alleged?
Does tenure overlap the alleged events?
Is knowledge firsthand or hearsay, and who is the underlying source?
What dated facts and corroborating documents connect the account to a defendant?

factors.label: Accounting & restatement
factors.description: Identify the accounting rule, transactions, amount and alleged contemporaneous knowledge; a restatement is not itself fraud.
questions: Which accounting treatment or GAAP rule was allegedly violated?
What period and financial line items changed?
Are the allegations about falsity distinguished from scienter?

factors.label: Executive departures
factors.description: Timing and circumstances of departures, with causal connection to the alleged misconduct kept explicit.
questions: Who departed, when and for what stated reason?
What sourced allegation links the departure to misconduct?

factors.label: Core operations
factors.description: Importance of operations plus specific exposure to relevant information; position alone does not establish knowledge.
questions: How central was the operation and how unusual was the event?
What specifically connects senior management to the relevant information?

factors.label: Parallel regulatory action
factors.description: Track allegations, investigations, charges and findings separately; an inquiry is not a finding of scienter.
questions: Which agency, action and date?
Was there an inquiry, charge, settlement without admission, or adjudicated finding?
Does it concern the same conduct and individuals?

factors.label: Contemporaneous knowledge
factors.description: Reports, meetings and communications linking contradictory information to a defendant at the statement date.
questions: What information contradicted which public statement?
Who received it, on what date, and how is receipt supported?

factors.label: Motive & opportunity
factors.description: Concrete personal benefit and means, distinguished from incentives common to ordinary corporate officers.
questions: What concrete personal benefit is alleged?
Is the incentive particularized or generally shared by corporate officers?

factors.label: Timing of events
factors.description: Record chronology without treating proximity or hindsight as proof of earlier knowledge.
questions: When were statement, warning, trade and correction made?
Does the source support earlier knowledge rather than hindsight?

factors.label: Magnitude & duration
factors.description: Record denominators, affected periods and duration; do not substitute magnitude for knowledge.
questions: What amount and percentage of the relevant financial metric were affected?
What are the statement and class periods, and how long did the conduct persist?

factors.label: Defendant attribution
factors.description: Separate each individual’s alleged state of mind from corporate attribution; corporate pleading can differ.
questions: Which statement and alleged knowledge belong to each defendant?
Whose intent is alleged to be imputable to the corporation and why?

factors.label: Opposing inferences
factors.description: Preserve supported nonculpable explanations and the court’s collective evaluation; never total factors into a scienter verdict.
questions: What plausible competing explanations does the opinion identify?
How does the court assess all allegations together?

2.title: Second Circuit · PSLRA strong inference
2.summary: Tellabs requires a holistic comparison against plausible nonculpable inferences. Second Circuit decisions describe motive and opportunity or strong circumstantial evidence of conscious misbehavior or recklessness; generalized corporate motives are insufficient. Corporate attribution is distinct from naming an individual defendant. Research orientation only: this draft is not an exhaustive current-law treatment or citator check.

9.title: Ninth Circuit · intentional conduct or deliberate recklessness
9.summary: Apply Tellabs holistically alongside the Ninth Circuit’s particularity requirements for intentional conduct or deliberate recklessness. Zucco distinguishes CW reliability and personal knowledge from whether the statements indicate scienter. Core-operations allegations require context. Research orientation only: this draft is not an exhaustive current-law treatment or citator check.
